i hate lens flare.

lens flare happens when you're looking through a fucking lens. it doesn't happen when you're looking at cool mountains in the distance unless you are looking at them via a lens of some sort. it shouldn't happen when you're dramatically framing a location for narrative purposes.

every damn time i see a lens flare used it takes me out of the movie, reminding me that there is a camera in some studio back lot or on location breaking the fourth wall for no purpose whatsoever except to show how artistic and clever the cinematographer or director is.

the fact that an artificial artifact like lens flare is used intentionally to establish a sense of realism is so perverse that it is, in my opinion, the single most prescient example of how doomed the human race is and how little hope each of us should have for the future.

it would be like an author placing a photograph of a typewriter on every page in a book where they are describing a location, or an obnoxious audible reminder every time your favorite band uses software to correct the very human mistakes musicians regularly make when they play together every time you hear that great song you love. it is the movie equivalent of a sitcom character's catchphrase and should be impressive only to very young children.

to summarize, lens flare is an unnecessary and indulgent stylistic flourish that serves no purpose beyond self-indulgence and people who like it will have to work a tiny bit harder to earn my respect.
I get that 4th wall reaction to it as well. It's a tacky attempt to lull you into the message of the movie. Kudos to us to be awake when it happens.
